name: Robert Nozick
worldviewSummary: In Anarchy, State, and Utopia Nozick argues that individuals have rights that function as side-constraints, so only a minimal state limited to protection against force, theft and fraud is justified. Justice in holdings is historical: whatever arises from just acquisition by just transfer is just, so patterned redistribution violates rights. His experience-machine thought experiment challenges the idea that only felt experience matters.
biography: American philosopher at Harvard. Anarchy, State, and Utopia (1974) won the National Book Award; his later work ranged widely, and in The Examined Life (1989) he distanced himself from aspects of his earlier libertarianism.

concepts.description: A distribution is just if it arose through just acquisition, just transfer, and rectification of past injustice — regardless of the resulting pattern.
If a machine could give you any experiences you desired, would you plug in for life? Most would not, suggesting we care about actually doing things and being certain kinds of people.
Rights limit what may be done to persons rather than being goals to maximize; individuals may not be sacrificed for others' ends.

positions.statement: Taxation of earnings from labour is on a par with forced labour, since it takes the fruits of a person's work without consent.
Through the Wilt Chamberlain example, liberty upsets patterns: voluntary transfers will disrupt any favoured distribution unless the state continually interferes.
A minimal state limited to protection against force, theft and fraud and enforcement of contracts is justified; any more extensive state violates rights.
What matters is not only how our lives feel from the inside; we want to do certain things, be certain sorts of people, and be in contact with a deeper reality.

relations.note: Chapter 7 of Anarchy, State, and Utopia criticizes Rawls's difference principle.

constraints.rule: Ground libertarian positions in Anarchy, State, and Utopia, and acknowledge that Nozick later qualified some of these views.
